Northern Europe's biggest man-made lake is in Northumberland 💧
Kielder Water can hold 200 billion litres. The Queen opened it on 26 May 1982 after seven years of building at a cost of £167m. It has 27 miles of shoreline, is 52 metres deep at its deepest, and tunnels link the Tyne with the Wear, Derwent and Tees so its water can be released into all four rivers. The scheme can supply up to 909 million litres a day.
